Nakamura is one of the devil hunters stationed along Denji's patrol route, and when Santa Claus attacks Denji's group with his dolls, Nakamura defends them by using his Fox Devil contract. Nakamura then calls the Public Safety HQ for backup, before he is quickly decapitated by Quanxi in her massacre.

entities.description:
Nobana bears a notable resemblance to Kobeni, especially his face and eyes. Similarly to Kobeni he also has moles on his face, precisely two just under his right eye. He has short, brown hair that is kept in line by six hair clips on his right side and falls to his face on the left. Similarly to his sister, he is also quite short. Nobana wears the standard boys' uniform of Fourth East High School and has the typical cap from the Devil Hunter Club, though he sometimes wear it. He is always seen with sweat on his face, often also blushing.

Much like his older sister, Nobana is perpetually anxious but, unlike her, even more so and he hasn't had any moments of competency or bravery so far. He gets easily embarrassed and stutters uncontrollably when merely trying to say the word "sex". Similarly to Kobeni, his parents put a lot of pressure on him and force him to do activities he doesn't enjoy, like joining the Devil Hunter Club. Nobana's mind is fragile, as he goes insane after a few days of being trapped in the aquarium, licking the glass senselessly.

Later, Nobana joins the Chainsaw Man Church and becomes fully devoted to their cause, easily believing the lies which the Church tells its followers showing he's very susceptible to manipulation and conspiracy theories. For example, he believes that the concept of marrying as an adult is a system from the USA designed to control the Japanese like slaves and encourages students to have children and marry each other.

At some point in his life, Nobana was forced to join the Devil Hunter Club by his mother, as she believed it would earn him scholarships. He was also constantly picked on by various bullies who made him to light up their cigarettes with his lighter.

entities.name: Seraphim
entities.description:
A seraph (Hebrew: שָׂרָף, romanized: sārāf ; plural seraphim Hebrew: שְׂרָפִים, romanized: sərāfīm ) is a celestial or heavenly being originating in Ancient Judaism. The term plays a role in subsequent Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.

Tradition places seraphim in the highest rank in Christian angelology and in the fifth rank of ten in the Jewish angelic hierarchy. A seminal passage in the Book of Isaiah (Isaiah 6:1–8) used the term to describe six-winged beings that fly around the Throne of God crying out "holy, holy, holy". This throne scene, with its triple invocation of holiness, profoundly influenced subsequent theology, literature, and art. Its influence is frequently seen in works depicting angels, heaven, and apotheosis. Seraphim are mentioned as celestial beings in the semicanonical Book of Enoch and the canonical Book of Revelation.

His hair is trimmed short and neatly, with only a short tuft of hair coming down the left side of his fringe. His most notable feature is the stitched arc-shaped scar that wraps from his forehead, down his left eye and stopping short from the top of his lip. His intact eye is rather drowsy in appearance with notable eyebags, suggesting that the recent Devil attacks have taken a toll to his health.

Takagi is shown most in his element whenever he believes he has control over a situation and can order other, more powerful people to do his bidding in order to keep his hands clean. Without this control, his instinct is to either retreat and recuperate, or to violently snap.

His most notable trait is his relationship with his wife, whom had been transformed into a Pseudo-Chainsaw Man thanks to a Fire Devil contract. Despite claiming to love her and viewing her as a symbol of all that's good in the world, he still went behind her back and cheated on her, even dismissing his actions as not being severe due to how the affair only lasted half a year. In addition to how he treats his wife, he also appears to treat women as lesser beings, as his dying words implied he was about to say something sexist due to Quanxi's disobedience.

In spite of his "devotion" to his wife, he appears to be fairly apathetic to the suffering of others: he didn't object to any of Denji's organ harvesting despite how much pain it would've caused the boy, and when he found out his wife was turned into a devil, he instead wished his ornery neighbour should've transformed instead.

She stands at the top of the building that had been sent to hell and pulls out an arrow from under Quanxi's eyepatch. She then drops Quanxi's head to the fight that was occurring between Denji and Santa Claus below, allowing Quanxi to transform into her hybrid form and kill the dolls that were attacking Denji.

After Santa Claus has been dealt with. Makima appears out from the smoke, drawing her sword. Quanxi surrenders, pleading to Makima to not kill her women, even offering her own limbs so that she won't. However, her words are futile, and Makima kills Quanxi, Cosmo and Tsugihagi by decapitating them.

entities.name: Virtue
entities.description:
A virtue (Latin: virtus) is a trait of excellence, including traits that may be moral, social, or intellectual. The cultivation and refinement of virtue is held to be the "good of humanity" and thus is valued as an end purpose of life or a foundational principle of being. In human practical ethics, a virtue is a disposition to choose actions that succeed in showing high moral standards: doing what is said to be right and avoiding what is wrong in a given field of endeavour, even when doing so may be unnecessary from a utilitarian perspective. When someone takes pleasure in doing what is right, even when it is difficult or initially unpleasant, they can establish virtue as a habit. Such a person is said to be virtuous through having cultivated such a disposition. The opposite of virtue is vice.

Other examples of this notion include the concept of merit in Asian traditions as well as De (Chinese 德, "character," "integrity").

entities.description:
The Whip Hybrid (real name unknown) is a Devil-human Hybrid who merged with the の|Muchi no Akuma}} and serves as a minor antagonist in the Control Devil arc, where she faces the Chainsaw Devil.

She later returns in the Academy Saga as a supporting antagonist, working under the orders of Barem and the Chainsaw Man Church alongside her other fellow Weapon Humans.

The Whip Hybrid is a woman of short stature with messy, shoulder-length brown hair and bangs covering her forehead. Additionally, she also has dark, almost smudged circles under her eyes. In most of her appearances, the Whip Hybrid wears a long blazer over a button-up shirt, draped loosely over her shoulders like a cape. Her shirt is tucked into a pair of dark high-waisted pants and paired with shoes. She notably dons a pair of circular shades and is the shortest in stature amongst the other Hybrids.

During her time as one of Makima's brainwashed servants, the Whip Hybrid wore the standard Public Safety Devil Hunter suit and tie. Even when being mind-controlled, she chose to wear the coat of her suit draped over her shoulders rather than wearing it properly.

She wears the same school uniform as the rest of the girls in her class. The uniform consists of a long-sleeved button up shirt worn beneath a pinafore style dress with a pleated skirt that extends below the knee, a bow at the collar, a wide belt at the waist, and white, knee-high socks. She also wears sneakers. When outside of school, she wears a blank shirt with a dark-colored jacket, light jeans that reach just slightly below the knees, and a pair of sandals.

The contract makes her capable of transforming herself into a thin and gaunt being with an uncovered brain and tentacles instead of legs.

When she's resurrected following her first death at the hands of Asa, Yuko comes back as a gigantic monster with the head of her transformed form surrounded by tentacles. In this form, she's big enough to cover several floors of the school with her body.

The |Zonbi no Akuma}} is a Devil who embodies the concept of zombies. He is the secondary antagonist of the Introduction arc, who turned various Yakuza into zombies and attempted to kill Denji.

The Zombie Devil takes the form of a giant floating limbless torso with multiple exposed organs including a brain from which tentacles emerge to connect him to zombies within his horde. A large human-like face emerges from the right side of the devil's torso unconnected to where its head should be. During the fight with Denji, he loses his right eye and is later cut into two halves.

The Zombie Devil has a greater hatred towards humans, particularly towards devil hunters. Since devil hunters killed his own kind, the Zombie Devil seeks to kill Devil Hunters in return. He appears to be somewhat cunning, since he managed to trick the Yakuza and turn them into zombies.

The Zombie Devil made a deal with a mafia group to lend them his power, but since his power turns people into zombies, they became his servants. He then called Denji to an abandoned building and made his new zombies kill him, since he hates devil hunters.

Makima, revealed to be Control, was the first Horseman to appear, and she made reference to the other three well before any of them made their debut. The four are some of the most prominent Devils featured in the Chainsaw Man manga, with Makima being the main antagonist of the Public Safety Saga while the other three (along with Nayuta, Makima's reincarnation) are among the main characters featured in Part 2, the Academy Saga; among the four, Yoru stands as the second saga's main antagonist.

The Horsemen are four particularly powerful Devils who take on the form of human females and consider themselves |shimai}}. Death is the eldest and most powerful, Fami (Famine) is the second-eldest, and Yoru (War) along with Nayuta (Control) are the youngest. While Nayuta is currently the youngest of the four as Makima's recently born reincarnation, it is not explicitly confirmed if Fami and Yoru are older than Makima was.

entities.name: Aging's World
entities.description:
Aging's World is a realm that appears as a lush forest with a lake, where time ceases to exist for the humans trapped there. The people trapped there lose their sense of thirst, hunger and are unable to die, while slowly going insane. Those who stay for extended periods of time, like 1,000 or 2,000 years, transform into trees. These "Tree-People" are essentially victims of the Aging Devil, their bodies slowly rotting and returning to the soil, until eventually merging with nature. When this process happens the trapped humans can return to their bodies in the real World. Devil Powers don't function in this world, as seen when Yoru tried to use her powers to escape but was unable to do so. Because of that, it's possible this world is in its own separate dimension instead of a realm in the real world.

According to the Aging Devil's Victim, there was someone who supposedly managed to escape this realm a long time ago.

During the fight between Pochita and Yoru both her and Asa Mitaka are sent to the Aging Devil's World, along with Yoshida and Denji. The Devil Hunters, including Denji, Asa and Yoru, face a powerful enemy sent by Public Safety, who can manipulate the concept of aging and is willing to sacrifice itself to be consumed by Chainsaw Man, hoping to trigger a new stage of human evolution, for humanity to have a standing chance against The Prophecy of Nostradamus, by removing the concept of aging.

Ultimately, they manage to trap the Aging Devil within its own realm, then they negotiate its return to Hell and escape successfully, while leaving Tadashi Hasegawa behind.

The チェンソーマン|Sekaiheiwa Chensōman Kyōkai}}, often referred to simply as the |Chensōman Kyōkai}} was a cult-like project developed by the Death Devil, Barem Bridge, Haruka Iseumi, and an unnamed elder.

Their stated intention was to aid Chainsaw Man in preventing the upcoming Age of Devils prophesied by Nostradamus and achieving a "world without evil". What they didn't tell their followers is that their plan was to sacrifice them en masse so that both Chainsaw Man and the War Devil become stronger through public fear to defeat the Death Devil.

"Fami" was the supposed brain and the true leader of the group, Barem being the one who enlisted people to make contracts with the Fire Devil, whilst Haruka's role was solely to attract more people to the cause. The role and identity of the fourth leader is not revealed. While Haruka was a member of the four "leaders", he wasn't fully aware of the meaning behind their actions. The Church also had many of the members of "The Weapons" among its top brass. Though, despite The Weapons' high position in the Church, they were disloyal to the Church, as Barem, one of the members of The Weapons, is seen asking Denji if killing Asa will bring back Chainsaw Man, and The Weapons were planning to lure Chainsaw Man out by massacring a bunch of civilian and Public Safety Devil Hunters despite the Church’s goal to stop him from fighting. Asa joined the Church under the promise of separating Chainsaw Man from his Devil heart, allowing Yoru to kill the Chainsaw Devil whilst Asa could live with "her" Chainsaw Man, as a compromise between the two. She was a Devil Hunter/Poster Girl for the Church and was paid with its donation money.

entities.description:
The |Tōkyō Akuma Shūyō}} is a large jail facility for Devils and those who have been affected by Devils located somewhere in Tokyo, Japan. It is the facility where Denji was temporarily held at in the Aging Devil arc after disobeying Public Safety's orders not to transform into Chainsaw Man.

The Detention Center is an incredibly large military facility. It sports large rectangular panels going across the walls of the building. Near the entrance are sensors that allow the control room to detect intruders that infiltrate the facility. The staff inside the control room can utilize the building's weapons such as gun turrets to kill off any intruders that attempt to enter the building.

Not much is known about the Detention Center, except that Devils who are considered too dangerous are sent here, and that not a single Devil since its inception has made it out alive.

After disobeying Public Safety's orders not to transform, Denji is sent to the Tokyo Devil Detention Center to be dismembered after having been heavily sedated for an entire week.
